name: W4 — Webhook to model to stored result

nodes.name: Webhook (header token)
nodes.notes:
THE TOKEN IS THE CONTROL, AND IT IS NOW BOUND. FOUND BY QA (NOM-302): this node said `authentication: headerAuth` with NO CREDENTIAL ATTACHED, which n8n treats as a configuration error — the webhook could not register, so the one security property this demo exists to show was absent. `aistack samples setup` generates a 48-hex-character token, writes it 0600 under secrets/ and imports it as the credential this node names; `aistack samples run W4` then POSTs with it, without it, and with a wrong one, and asserts 200/401/401 plus the row count after each.

THE TOKEN IS GENERATED, NEVER COMMITTED. Caddy proxies /n8n/webhook/* WITHOUT forward-auth — n8n's own header check is the only gate on that path — so a fixed token in git would be a shared secret published with the source.

responseMode is lastNode so the caller receives the stored row rather than n8n's 'workflow got started'. That is what makes the demo checkable from one HTTP call, and it is also the honest shape for a synchronous question-and-answer webhook.

LOCAL MODE ONLY, AND THE HARNESS PROVES IT RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT. Public webhooks are not in this release. `samples run W4` serves this workflow from a SHORT-LIVED helper n8n container on the internal networks, checks it there, and then checks that the live n8n — the one the reverse proxy talks to — still answers 404 on the same path. Caddy bounds the body to 1 MB before any of this runs.

nodes.name: Validate the request
nodes.notes: A length bound here as well as in Caddy. Caddy's 1 MB limit is about the cost of reading the request; this one is about the cost of the inference it would buy.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'local-chat', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: $json.prompt }], max_tokens: 160 }) }}

nodes.name: Ask the model via LiteLLM
nodes.notes: LiteLLM is the ONLY inference front door. n8n cannot reach Ollama directly — they share no network — and that is the point. MEASURED (NOM-302): LiteLLM answers 401 without a key, so the virtual key bound here is load-bearing and not decoration.

parameters.query: INSERT INTO w4_results (prompt, answer, created_at) VALUES ($1, $2, now()) RETURNING result_id, prompt, answer, created_at

nodes.name: Store the result
nodes.notes:
The demo role, which owns ONE database and is dropped by `samples teardown`. It is not the n8n operational role and it is not a superuser.

Both placeholders are bound through Query Parameters. FOUND BY QA (NOM-302): the first version wrote $1/$2 into the SQL and supplied nothing, so this statement could never have run — a prompt containing a quote would have been the second problem, had the first not been fatal.

This is the LAST node, so with responseMode=lastNode the stored row is what the caller gets back.
